Phosphine-catalyzed [3 + 2] cycloadditions of
triﬂuoromethyl enynes/enediynes with allenoates:
access to cyclopentenes containing a
CF3-substituted quaternary carbon center †
Shu-Jie Chen,
 a Guo-Shu Chen,a Jia-Wei Zhang,b Zhao-Dong Li,c
Yu-Lei Zhao
 d and Yun-Lin Liu
 *a
Herein, the ﬁrst use of tri ﬂuoromethyl-substituted enynes/enediynes as non-classical electron-de ﬁcient
oleﬁns for phosphine-catalyzed [3 + 2] cycloaddition with allenoates is reported. This reaction occurs
with excellent regioselectivity under mild conditions, a ﬀording alkyne- and diyne-tethered cyclopentene
derivatives containing a CF 3-substituted quaternary carbon center in moderate to good yields.
Five-membered carbocycles, including cyclopentenes and
cyclopentanes, are the key structural moieties of a number of
pharmaceuticals and bioactive natural and non-natural pro-
ducts (Fig. 1). 1 As a result, much attention has been devoted to
developing e ﬃcient strategies for the construction and
functionalization of cyclopentenes and cyclopentanes with
high structural diversity. 2 On the other hand, the trifluoro-
methyl (CF 3) group plays important roles in the pharma-
ceutical and agrochemical industries because trifluoromethyl-
ated compounds often display improved physicochemical and
biological properties compared to their non-fluorinated
counterparts.
3 For example, incorporating the trifluoromethyl
group into five-membered carbocycles has been found to
impart beneficial e ﬀects ( e.g. bioavailability and metabolic
stability) on many bioactive molecules (Fig. 1, bottom).
1e,f In
this context, the development of methods for the expedient
synthesis of CF
3-bearing five-membered carbocycles is highly
desirable.
Among the existing methodologies for the synthesis of
functionalized cyclopentenes, phosphine-catalyzed [3 + 2]
cycloaddition of allenoates with electron-deficient olefins first
reported by Lu ’s group in 1995 has shown notable e ﬃciency.4
Various olefins activated by one or more electron-withdrawing
groups, such as carbonyl, 5 phosphonyl,6 sulfonyl,7 cyano,8 and
nitro groups, 9 have been successfully applied to these cyclo-
addition processes (Scheme 1a). In contrast, trifluoromethyl
alkenes were less explored for this transformation. To the best
of our knowledge, there have been only two reports on the use
of trifluoromethyl alkenes as partners in Lu ’s [3 + 2] cyclo-
addition with allenes. Zhang ’s group reported chiral phos-
phine-catalyzed asymmetric [3 + 2] cycloadditions of
γ-substituted allenoates with β-trifluoromethyl enones, which
provided a facile access to highly functional trifluoromethyl-
ated cyclopentenes.
10 Loh and coworkers have demonstrated
two examples of phosphine-catalyzed [3 + 2] cycloaddition of
β-trifluoromethyl acrylates with aryl allenones (Scheme 1b). 11
In both reports, the CF 3 group only served as a second elec-
tron-withdrawing group and the application of trifluoromethyl
olefins without strong electron-withdrawing π-acceptors in

Lu’s [3 + 2] cycloaddition has not been realized so far. In fact,
only a palladium-catalyzed [3 + 2] cycloaddition of CF 3-substi-
tuted 1,3-enynes with trimethylenemethane (TMM) was
reported by Trost and coworkers in 2015, furnishing a facile
access to cyclopentenes bearing a CF
3-substituted quaternary
carbon center (Scheme 1c). 12
Recently, we found that CF 3-substituted enynes/enediynes
could undergo Michael-initiated ring-closure reactions with
sulfur ylides, furnishing alkyne- and diyne-tethered cyclopro-
panes bearing trifluoromethyl-substituted all-carbon quatern-
ary centers.
13 With our ongoing research interest in annulation
reactions14 and the development of practical syntheses of fluo-
rine-containing compounds, 15 we wondered whether the CF 3-
substituted enynes/enediynes would be applicable reaction
partners for Lu ’s [3 + 2] cycloaddition since the resulting pro-
ducts can serve as useful building blocks for further post-
functionalization through numerous metal- or organo-cata-
lyzed reactions. Herein we present phosphine-catalyzed [3 + 2]
cycloadditions of allenoates with CF
3-substituted enynes/ene-
diynes, which give rise to alkyne- and diyne-tethered cyclopen-
tenes bearing a CF 3-substituted quaternary carbon center
(Scheme 1d).
Initial studies were carried out with allenoate 1a and CF 3-
substituted enyne 2a. The expected [3 + 2] cycloaddition pro-
ceeded smoothly with excellent regioselectivity in the presence
of 10 mol% PPh 3 in toluene at room temperature, giving
α-adduct 3aa in 76% yield (Table 1, entry 1). In order to
increase the yield, various solvents were then examined,
among which both THF and EtOAc gave improved yields while
EtOH led to no reaction (entries 2 –6). In view of its environ-
mental benignity, EtOAc was selected as the optimal solvent
for this reaction. Next, a number of commercially available
mono- and bisphosphines were surveyed. Among those,
(4-MeOC
6H4)3P gave a better yield than (4-FC 6H4)3P (entries 7
and 8). PPh 2Me a ﬀorded 3aa in a yield comparable to that of
PPh3, while PBu 3 led to the rapid decomposition of the start-
ing material (entries 9 and 10). Bisphosphines, such as DPPF,
BINAP, and DPPP (1,3-bis(diphenylphosphino) propane), were
either less e ﬀective than PPh
3 or ine ﬀective (entries 11 –13).
When DABCO (1,4-diazabicyclo[2.2.2]octane) was used, the
α-adduct 3aa was obtained in 32% yield with >20 : 1 regio-
selectivity (entry 14).
Having established the optimal reaction conditions, the
scope of this [3 + 2] cycloaddition was then probed (Table 2).
First, various 2-trifluoromethyl-1,3-enynes were investigated. In
general, the electronic nature of substituents on the aromatic
rings had little e ﬀect on the regioselectivity but noticeable
influences on the yields. The enynes bearing electron-with-
drawing groups on the para- and ortho-positions of the phenyl
ring exhibited higher reactivities toward this cycloaddition,
giving the desired products ( 3aa–3af, 3am) in moderate to
good yields (62 –88%). CF
3-Enynes with a phenyl or tolyl
moiety turned out to be less reactive, a ﬀording products 3ag
and 3ah in 56% and 50% yields, respectively, under modified
conditions. Moreover, CF 3-enynes with the electron-withdraw-
ing group ( –NO2 or –F) and the electron-donating group ( –Me,
–OMe) on the meta-position of the phenyl ring were all toler-
ant, and the corresponding products 3ai–3al were obtained in
60–73% yields. In the case of disubstituted and fused-ring aro-
matic substrates, the desired products 3an–3ap were produced
in 51 –75% yields. To our delight, substrates containing a het-
eroaromatic ring (thiophene, benzofuran, indole, and carba-
zole) on the alkyne moiety were also applicable, and the
desired products ( 3aq–3at) were obtained in moderate to good
yields. However, alkyl-substituted CF 3-enyne, as well as CF 3-
styrene and CF 3-diene, failed to undergo this [3 + 2] cyclo-

addition with 1a. In addition, the substrate scope with respect
to the allenoate was examined. Other allenoates, such as
benzyl-, cyclohexyl-, and tert-butyl 2,3-butadienoates, proved to
be suitable substrates, a ﬀording the corresponding products
3ba–3da in 86–93% yields with an α/γ ratio of >20 : 1.
Encouraged by these results, we further extended our
studies to the synthesis of diyne-tethered cyclopentenes via
the cycloaddition of CF 3-enediynes (Table 3). 16 The CF 3-ene-
diynes bearing an electron-withdrawing group (Br) and an
electron-donating group (Me) on the para-position of the
phenyl ring were applicable, and the desired products 6a and
6b were obtained in 75% and 92% yields, respectively. To our
delight, alkyl CF 3-enediynes also proved to be competent sub-
strates toward this cycloaddition, a ﬀording the corresponding
adducts in good yields ( 6c–6f ). Notably, the acetone-derived
protecting groups were tolerated under the optimal con-
ditions, which provide feasibility for further structural elabor-
ations ( 6e and 6f ).
13b However, TIPS-protected enediyne
failed to give the target compound ( 6g). In addition, several
diﬀerent cl asses of allenes were also evaluated by using
p-tolyl-substituted CF 3-enediyne 5b as the reaction partner.
The reaction occurred readily in the case of α-trimethylsilyl-
substituted aryl allenone 1e,11 giving the desired
α-cycloadduct 6h, along with γ-cycloadduct 6i, in 48% and
32% yields, respectively. The α-methyl/benzyl-substituted
allenoates ( 1f and 1g) proved to be completely unreactive,
w h i l et h eu s eo f γ-methyl/phenyl-substituted allenoates ( 1h
and 1i) resulted in the formation of a complex mixture under
standard conditions.
To showcase the practicability of this [3 + 2] cycloaddition, a
gram-scale synthesis of CF 3-substituted cyclopentene 3ae was
performed. As illustrated in Scheme 2, the reaction was con-

ducted with 2-trifluoromethyl-1,3-enyne 2e (0.92 g, 4 mmol)
with only 1.5 equivalents of allenoate 1a (0.67 g, 6 mmol). The
reaction proceeded smoothly, a ﬀording the corresponding
product 3ae with a yield (86%, 1.18 g) comparable to that of the
small-scale reaction (Scheme 2, eqn (1)). The generated 3ae
could serve as a Michael acceptor undergoing Cu-catalysed
Michael addition with ethylmagnesium bromide to provide
cyclopentane 7 with 62% yield and a 2 : 1 dr value (Scheme 2,
eqn (2)).
5a The ester group of 3ae could be selectively reduced to
the alcohol in 89% yield with diisobutyl aluminium hydride
(DIBAL-H), and the resulting allylic alcohol 8 could be further
transferred into protected allylic amine 9 via the Mitsunobu
reaction with phthalimide (Scheme 2, eqn (3)). 17 In addition,
the hydrolyzation of cyclopentene 3ba into dicarboxylic acid 10
was achieved in 95% yield (Scheme 2, eqn (4)). The structure of
compound 10 was unambiguously confirmed by X-ray single-
crystal analysis (CCDC 2004999 †). Finally, the elaboration of
product 6f was performed to demonstrate the synthetic utility of
the alkyne functionality. The acetone-derived protecting group
on 6f was removed by treating with NaOH, and the resulting
terminal alkyne could further undergo azide –alkyne Huisgen
cycloaddition, giving the 1,2,3-triazole 11 in 57% yield over two
steps (Scheme 2, eqn (5)).
On the basis of the reported literature
18 and our experi-
mental findings, a stepwise mechanism is proposed in
Scheme 3. Initially, nucleophilic addition of phosphine onto
allenoate 1 forms the reactive zwitterionic intermediate Int-A,
which then undergoes α-addition to the double bond of 2-tri-
fluoromethyl-1,3-enyne 2 to yield the propargylic anion inter-
mediate Int-B or 1,2-allenic anion intermediate Int-C.
Subsequent intramolecular conjugate addition of Int-B occurs
to form the cyclic ylide intermediate Int-D. Finally, a [1,2]
proton transfer followed by β-elimination of the catalyst gives
rise to the target cyclopentene 3 with the concurrent release of
PPh3. The introduction of acetylene was key for a number of
reasons: (a) the electron-withdrawing polarization of ethynyl
groups may further activate CF
3-enynes for nucleophilic
addition by the zwitterionic intermediate 19 and (b) ethynyl
groups may help to stabilize the α-trifluoromethyl carbanion
species electronically, thus facilitating the ring closure
process.20
Conclusions
In conclusion, we have described the first phosphine-catalyzed
[3 + 2] cycloaddition of 2-trifluoromethyl enynes/enediynes
with allenoates, a ﬀording cyclopentenes containing a CF 3-sub-
stituted quaternary carbon center in moderate to high yields
and with excellent regioselectivity. Furthermore, several elabor-
ations based on the generated products were conducted to
demonstrate their synthetic potential. This methodology suc-
cessfully expanded the substrate scope of Lu ’s [3 + 2] cyclo-
addition with respect to electron-deficient olefins. The readily
available catalyst, environment friendly solvent, and excellent
regioselectivity make it a practical and expedient approach
for accessing biologically important trifluoromethylated
cyclopentenes.
